metadata.gitb:name: Patient (Dynamic SUT Round-Trip via System Parameter)
metadata.gitb:description: Confirms that a Patient resource submitted through the ITB is actually persisted by, and retrievable from, the real SUT being certified. The target endpoint is not hardcoded in this test case — it's read from the "sutEndpoint" system configuration parameter bound to whichever system is under test for this session ($SYSTEM{sutEndpoint}, a GITB-native per-system config value set once per SUT by an admin in gitb-ui when its conformance statement is configured — see docs.itb.ec.europa.eu/docs/tdl/latest/expressions). ITB forwards the create there, then GETs the resource back by the ID the SUT assigned and compares the family name to confirm the round trip worked — one test case, reusable across every SUT, no per-system TDL file needed.

process.desc: Extract family name from the submitted payload, to check against the read-back

send.desc: Forward new patient to the SUT under test — endpoint read from this system's sutEndpoint configuration parameter

process.desc: Extract the server-assigned ID — this step itself fails the test case if the create response body did not include one

send.desc: Retrieve the patient back from the SUT by ID — a capability every SUT must support

verify.desc: Validate the patient could be retrieved back by ID

process.desc: Extract family name from the retrieved payload

verify.desc: Confirm the retrieved patient's family name matches what was submitted, proving the write was persisted correctly and is readable by ID

success.default: "Patient " || $sutPatientId || " created on " || $SYSTEM{shortName} || "'s SUT (HTTP " || $createStatus || ") and retrieved by ID; family name matched: " || $retrievedFamilyName

failure.default: "Dynamic SUT round trip failed for system " || $SYSTEM{shortName} || " — endpoint=" || $SYSTEM{sutEndpoint} || ", create HTTP " || $createStatus || ", read HTTP " || $lastStatus || " - " || $lastBody
